items.headline: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers Jackson Hole debut speech; futures slip as traders wait
items.why: First Jackson Hole address from a new Fed chair is the single largest rate-path repricing event of the quarter. A hawkish read compresses multiples on long-duration tech; a dovish read is a broad risk-on trigger. Positioning is defensive into it.

items.headline: Core PCE stuck at 3.3% — disinflation has stalled, not reversed
items.why: The Fed's preferred gauge holding at 3.3% removes the case for a near-term cut. Rate-cut odds for the Sept 15-16 FOMC have already collapsed to ~33%. Directly negative for long-duration growth and small caps; supportive for the dollar.

items.headline: Nvidia annual revenue doubles, guides solidly into 2028 — stock +6%
items.why: A guide that extends visibility to 2028 is the strongest possible signal that AI capex is not rolling over. This is the anchor datapoint for the entire semi and AI-infrastructure complex, and it re-rates the supply chain, not just NVDA.

items.headline: Marvell tumbles 14% — adjusted EPS of $0.67 on $2.01B revenue only matched estimates
items.why: Revenue rose 58% on strong AI demand for custom silicon, yet an in-line print was punished with a 14% drawdown. The read-through: the bar for AI-adjacent names is now a beat-and-raise, not a beat. Watch for the same setup in other custom-ASIC names.

items.headline: Software rips: Salesforce +20%, Okta +26%, CrowdStrike results bolster the sector
items.why: A 20% move in a mega-cap like CRM is a violent sentiment reset for enterprise software, which had been the market's funding source all summer. Suggests AI monetization is finally showing up in seat-based and consumption revenue.

items.headline: Futures price just 32.6% odds of a cut at the September 15-16 FOMC
items.why: Traders have sharply pulled back easing expectations. Small caps and regional-rate-sensitive financials carry the most downside if this drifts toward zero; a Warsh surprise today is the main upside risk to this pricing.

items.headline: Super Micro rallies 6% on Q1 guidance far above consensus ($14.5-15.5B rev vs $11.7B est.)
items.why: A ~30% revenue guide-above-consensus from the primary AI server integrator corroborates the Nvidia demand signal from the systems side. EPS guided $1.01-1.10 vs $0.76 consensus.

items.headline: Maersk hikes 2026 guidance a second time as Strait of Hormuz blockade snarls global trade; shares +7%
items.why: A sustained Hormuz disruption is a structural bid under crude and a tax on goods inflation. Energy majors are the direct beneficiary; it simultaneously worsens the core-PCE problem the Fed is already stuck on.

items.headline: Atlassian +29% on Q4 revenue and earnings beat, though FY growth of 13% just missed
items.why: Part of the same software re-rating as CRM/OKTA. Notable that the market looked through a slight full-year growth miss — sentiment, not fundamentals, was the constraint.

items.headline: Ross Stores +8% premarket on Q2 beat and above-consensus Q3 guidance
items.why: Off-price retail outperforming is a classic late-cycle tell — the consumer is trading down but still spending. Mildly supportive for TJX and WMT, mildly negative for full-price discretionary.
